title: [AUG-105] Recording source switcher: browser picker vs direct system audio capture
why_we_need_this:
Outcome of brainstorm AUG-103. Today system audio is captured only via getDisplayMedia() in the browser (@client/src/components/FileUpload.tsx, ~L336), so every dual-track recording forces the user through the screen picker and share confirmation. On Windows this is an acceptable compromise; on macOS it is needless friction.

Constraint discovered during the brainstorm: August is a plain Vite + React web client, not Electron. A browser page can never receive system audio without the picker. The only component that runs with OS-level access is the local Node server (it already spawns whisper-cli and ffmpeg). Therefore "direct" capture must be server-side: the server captures system audio into a file and the client attaches it as the existing audio-system track, so mergeDualStream and the [Me]/[Them] pipeline stay unchanged.

Chosen design (phase 1, macOS first):
1. New preference field systemAudioSource: 'auto' | 'browser' | 'system' (default 'auto') in @client/src/services/preferences.ts and the allow-list in @server/src/routes/preferences.ts. Keep the existing systemAudio boolean as the on/off switch; the new field only chooses HOW system audio is captured.
2. Settings modal (@client/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx, Recording section, next to the System Audio toggle): dropdown "System audio source" with Auto / Browser (screen picker) / System (direct). Follow the SettingsDropdown pattern already used for Recording Mode. Brutalist style: 0 border-radius.
3. Server capability probe GET /api/capture/capabilities returning { systemCapture: boolean, method: 'coreaudio-tap' | 'blackhole' | 'none', platform, hint }. Detection pattern: same execFile-on-PATH approach as checkFfmpegAvailable in @server/src/services/whisper.ts. Settings shows the result inline under the dropdown ("System capture: available" / "needs setup: <hint>"); the System option is disabled when not available.
4. Server capture lifecycle: POST /api/capture/start -> { captureId, startedAt }, POST /api/capture/stop -> writes the file and returns { captureId, path, durationMs }. Endpoints are loopback-only like the rest of the server. Implementation on macOS: ffmpeg -f avfoundation reading a loopback input (BlackHole virtual device), or a Core Audio process-tap helper CLI when present (macOS 14.2+; verify the exact binary and flags during implementation). Orphaned captures (client crashed) are stopped and cleaned on server start.
5. Client wiring in FileUpload.tsx: when systemAudio is on and the resolved source is 'system', skip getDisplayMedia, call /api/capture/start alongside the mic MediaRecorder, and on stop call /api/capture/stop; the session upload references the server-side file as the system track instead of uploading a Blob (extend @server/src/routes/sessions.ts to accept a captureId in place of the systemAudio multipart file). Record wall-clock start timestamps on both tracks so the server can offset-align them before mergeDualStream.
6. Resolution of 'auto': system when the capability probe says available, otherwise browser. Windows resolves to browser in phase 1 (no regression).
7. Fallback: if /api/capture/start fails, fall back to the browser picker and show a toast explaining why; the recording still proceeds.
8. Live transcription mode (ScriptProcessorNode tap of the display stream) keeps using the browser path in phase 1; when source resolves to 'system' and recordingMode is 'live', show a notice and use browser capture for that recording. Follow-up task may move live chunking server-side.

Out of scope (follow-ups noted in AUG-103 brainstorm): Windows WASAPI loopback helper; Chrome auto-select flags in start.bat; keeping the display stream alive between recordings to ask the picker once per app session.
acceptance_criteria:
- A macOS user with the capture helper installed sets System audio source = System, presses Record once, and gets a dual-track session with [Me]/[Them] labels and no screen picker or share confirmation.
- With source = Browser, behaviour is identical to today (getDisplayMedia picker), on both platforms.
- With source = Auto on Windows, or on macOS without the helper, recording uses the browser picker and the Settings row states why System is unavailable.
- Settings > Recording shows a "System audio source" dropdown (Auto / Browser / System) with the capability status line under it; the choice persists across reloads via PATCH /api/preferences.
- GET /api/capture/capabilities, POST /api/capture/start and POST /api/capture/stop exist, are documented in the server routes, and are reachable only on loopback.
- If server capture fails to start, the recording falls back to the browser picker with a visible toast, and no session is lost.
- Server-captured system track and browser mic track are offset-aligned so a spoken word on one side does not appear more than ~500 ms out of order in the merged transcript.
- Crash recovery: an orphaned server capture is cleaned up on server restart; the existing IndexedDB mic recovery still works.
- project-context/preferences and project-context/architecture READMEs document the new field, the capture endpoints and the browser-only constraint.
